title: Chronic Diarrhea
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with severe, refractory peptic ulcer disease, chronic watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, and GI bleeding. Multiple ulcers in atypical locations (distal duodenum, jejunum). ZES is caused by a gastrin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor (gastrinoma) — most commonly in the duodenum or pancreas → massive gastric acid hypersecretion → severe PUD and diarrhea (acid inactivates pancreatic enzymes + damages mucosa). Often associated with MEN1. Diagnosis: fasting serum gastrin level — markedly elevated (>1000 pg/mL or >10x normal). If borderline → secretin stimulation test (paradoxical increase in gastrin in ZES). Localize tumor: somatostatin receptor scintigraphy (Octreoscan), CT/MRI, EUS. Treatment: high-dose PPI (omeprazole, pantoprazole) to control acid hypersecretion. Surgical resection if localized. If metastatic or unresectable → long-term PPI + octreotide.
chief_complaint: Severe PUD, chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain
